etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English yes, from Old English ġīese (“by all means, of course, yes”), derived from the same root as yea.

definitions.definition: An exclamation of pleasure or approval, usually transcribed with an exclamation point.
Response that confirms that the user is paying attention.
(interrogative) Used to ask for more information with a request.
An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.
A vote of support or in favor/favour of something.
(colloquial, transitive) To agree with, affirm, approve.

quote.citation: 1972 Oct, John Barth, “Perseid”, in Harper's Magazine, page 79:
quote.text: "That's really what you wanted?" I yessed both; ...

definitions.definition: (slang) To attempt to flatter someone by habitually agreeing
